items.title: Meta shipped an 816B open model
items.oneliner: Meta's 816B Muse Spark Open runs on two Mac Studios, making frontier-scale local inference suddenly less absurd.

items.title: Google launched Deep Review
items.oneliner: Google's Deep Review gives two free technical document reviews weekly, pushing automated paper and spec critique into normal workflows.

items.title: AI coding sped output but slowed review
items.oneliner: Harvard found coding agents raised output 30%, but review time jumped 49%, so velocity gains still hit human bottlenecks.

items.title: OpenBSD carried a 37-year-old root bug
items.oneliner: Researchers turned a 37-year-old OpenBSD integer overflow into root access, proving old kernel assumptions still break modern defenses.

items.title: Epic's Linux anti-cheat looks bypassable
items.oneliner: Epic's new Linux anti-cheat leans on TPM attestation, but researchers say runtime resets can still fake trusted boots.

items.title: Prompt traces can leak company secrets
items.oneliner: Origin says models can recover private company rules from prompt traces, turning everyday AI logs into an exfiltration surface.

items.title: ChatGPT ads can target prompt context
items.oneliner: 404 Media showed ChatGPT ads can target by prompts, email, and phone-linked identity, collapsing the privacy fiction around chats.

items.title: Accenture capped Claude spending
items.oneliner: Accenture now limits centrally paid Claude access to $29 per employee monthly, a clear sign AI usage bills are getting real.

items.title: Scraping pressure is forcing defensive internet economics
items.oneliner: Meta's new terms and smarter scrapers are pushing publishers toward paywalls, because open web traffic is becoming impossible to trust.

items.title: Iroh reached 1.0 after leaving IPFS
items.oneliner: Iroh hit 1.0 by dropping strict IPFS compatibility, a pragmatic reminder that shipping often beats protocol purity.
